summary: Waren Spacefarer, a young pilot with ten credits, wants forty thousand to buy Marta Okafor's Kestrel. His relief pilot job on Dren Vasko's tug Grubstake turned out to be people smuggling. He alerted customs, disabled the drive, got Vasko to surrender, freed eleven refugees and filed an informant claim (payout months away). He took Juno Reyes's three-hundred-credit medicine run to Occator Ridge, landed blind in the dust and broke the weak starboard strut. The hab crew anchored the tilting skiff and took the medicine inside. Now Juno is calling after seeing the telemetry. His pay and the steady work she promised depend on that call.

facts: Marta Okafor will sell the Kestrel to Waren for forty thousand credits.
Vasko promised Waren six hundred credits on delivery to Vesta.
Waren killed the Grubstake's main drive breaker; the tug can't burn.
Vasko surrendered and wants customs told it was all his doing.
Eleven refugees from the Grubstake hold are now in customs custody.
A customs informant fund pays only after a statement, a conviction and a review, months away.
Waren filed an informant fund claim; any payout is months away.
The refugee woman with the toddler asked for Waren's name.
Waren accepted Juno's Occator Ridge run: three hundred cash on landing.
The ridge pad approach: come in low from the north, mind the hab mast at forty metres.
The skiff is anchored on the Occator Ridge pad with a broken starboard strut.

recent.action: Ask about the short-hop courier job
recent.narration:
You tap the listing. A minute later a woman calls the hall screen back: mid-thirties, headset, a dock bay full of noise behind her.

"Juno Reyes, Reyes Rapid. My pilot quit an hour ago." She squints at your license scan. "Licensed, young, cheap. Good. A sealed medical crate to the mining hab at Occator Ridge. Fast skiff, nasty terrain, the landing pad's half a ledge. Three hundred cash on landing."

She sees you hesitate. "It's real medicine, kid. Customs already scanned it. I saw where you're calling from."

Then she adds, "Fly it clean and I've got steadier work. Real money for a pilot who doesn't crash my skiffs."

Bay Nine. She wants an answer now.

recent.action: Take the job, head to Bay Nine
recent.narration:
"I'll take it." Juno grins and cuts the call.

Bay Nine is cold and smells of coolant. It's crammed with three stubby courier skiffs, and one of them is scarred along the belly like it has scraped a few ledges already. Juno meets you at the hatch and slaps a sealed white crate strapped in the cargo net.

"Insulin and antibiotics. The ridge hab's out of both." She hands you a datapad with the approach chart. "Crosswinds don't exist on Ceres, but the dust does. Kicks up off the pad and blinds your sensors at the last fifty metres. Last guy bent a strut."

The skiff's controls are worn smooth. Your hands settle on them like they've always lived there.
recent.picture: Cramped cold docking bay with three stubby courier skiffs, one with a scarred belly. A lean young man in his early twenties, short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt, cargo pants and scuffed boots, takes a datapad from a woman in her mid-thirties, athletic build, sharp tanned face, dark curly hair tied back, quick brown eyes, red work vest over a black thermal shirt, headset, beside a sealed white crate. Harsh work lights.

recent.narration:
You sit with the datapad on your knee and trace the approach. The ridge pad sticks out from a crater wall, and there's a long shadow to the east where your sensors will be useless. Someone has scrawled a note in the margin: "Come in from the north, low. Watch the hab mast at forty metres." It means flying by eye for the last stretch. You can do that.

Juno leans in the hatch. "Clock's running, kid."

recent.action: Run a quick preflight check on the strut
recent.narration:
You crouch under the scarred belly and run your hand along the starboard strut. It's a fresh weld, rough but solid, and the damper hisses a little too softly when you lean on it. It will hold one landing if you put her down gently, maybe not a hard one.

Juno taps the hatch frame. "Well?"

The skiff leaps off the ring, and Ceres swells grey beneath you. You come in from the north, low, and pass the hab mast with room to spare. Then the dust rises like a curtain, and your sensors go blank.

You fly by eye. For a moment it's perfect. Then a pocket of loose regolith slides under the port pad, and the skiff drops a hand's width onto the starboard strut.

The weld cracks. The damper bursts with a shriek. The skiff lurches sideways and your ribs slam into the harness as the starboard side sags toward the edge of the ledge. Beyond it is nothing but crater shadow.

The engines are still idling and the crate is still strapped in behind you. Through the dust, figures in pressure suits are running from the hab lock.
recent.picture: A stubby courier skiff with a scarred belly tilting dangerously on a narrow landing ledge jutting from a grey crater wall on Ceres, broken starboard landing strut, grey dust swirling, black starry sky. Inside the cockpit a lean young man in his early twenties, short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt, grips the controls. Distant figures in pressure suits run from a hab airlock.

recent.action: Radio the hab crew for anchors
recent.narration:
You key the open channel and keep your voice flat. "Skiff on the pad, starboard strut gone. I need anchors on the port side, now. Nobody near the starboard edge."

A gravelly voice answers. "Copy, pilot. Hold her steady." Three suited figures crouch low and haul cable from the hab lock. They spike two ground anchors into the rock and snap the lines onto your port tie-downs. The cables go taut and the skiff groans, then settles. It's crooked, but it's not going anywhere.

You kill the engines. Your hands are shaking now that they're allowed to.

The crew unloads the white crate and hurries it inside. A minute later your comm blinks. It's Bay Nine, Juno Reyes, and she has already seen the telemetry.

action: Answer Juno and own the strut
